newsitem.title: GERMANY: German building union confirms wage deal approved.
newsitem.headline: German building union confirms wage deal approved.

text.p: A spokesman for German construction union IG Bau on Friday confirmed that the union's wages commission had approved a wage settlement reached in talks with employers on Friday.
A clear majority in the commission was in favour of accepting the deal, a union spokesman said.
The commission is made of up regional union representatives and its approval is needed for any deal to be finally accepted.
The compromise deal reached on Friday offers better sick pay benefits than an earlier proposed deal. It means a strike in the sector has now been averted.

The deal cuts pay for the first three days of sickness to 80 percent of full pay whereas an earlier agreement reached after arbitration talks planned to cut sick pay for the first three weeks of illness.
The commission had on Monday rejected that agreement, prompting further negotiations.
In return, holiday bonuses will be reduced to 25 percent of monthly pay from 30 percent. Both employers' federations have already agreed to the pact.
